## Purpose and Scope

This document covers BioJava's computational tools for analyzing protein surface areas and molecular interfaces. The system provides algorithms for calculating Accessible Surface Area (ASA) using the rolling ball method, detecting contacts between molecular chains, and identifying crystal interfaces through symmetry operations. For structure visualization and display components, see [Jmol Integration and Structure Visualization](#5.1). For protein comparison applications, see [Protein Comparison Tool](#5.2).

## ASA Calculation System

### Core ASA Algorithm

The `AsaCalculator` class implements the Shrake-Rupley rolling ball algorithm for computing Accessible Surface Areas. The algorithm samples points on a sphere around each atom and determines which points are accessible (not occluded by neighboring atoms).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Structure["Structure Input"] --> AsaCalc["AsaCalculator"]
    AsaCalc --> SphereGen["generateSpherePoints()"]
    AsaCalc --> NeighborFind["findNeighborIndices()"]
    AsaCalc --> RadiusLookup["getRadius()"]
    
    SphereGen --> GoldenSpiral["Golden Section Spiral<br/>Algorithm"]
    NeighborFind --> SpatialHash["Spatial Hashing Grid"]
    NeighborFind --> AllToAll["All-to-All Distance"]
    RadiusLookup --> ChothiaRadii["Chothia VDW Radii"]
    
    GoldenSpiral --> AsaCalcSingle["calcSingleAsa()"]
    SpatialHash --> AsaCalcSingle
    ChothiaRadii --> AsaCalcSingle
    
    AsaCalcSingle --> GroupAsa["GroupAsa Results"]
    AsaCalcSingle --> AtomAsa["Per-Atom ASA Values"]
```

**ASA Calculation Pipeline**

The system uses Van der Waals radii from Chothia (1976) to account for different atom types in amino acids and nucleotides. The `DEFAULT_N_SPHERE_POINTS` is set to 1000 for accuracy, with `DEFAULT_PROBE_SIZE` of 1.4 Å.

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/asa/AsaCalculator.java:55-669]()

### Spatial Optimization

The ASA calculator employs spatial hashing to efficiently find neighboring atoms within the cutoff distance, avoiding costly all-to-all distance calculations.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Atoms["Atom Coordinates"] --> Grid["Grid Spatial Hash"]
    Grid --> CellSize["Cell Size = Cutoff"]
    Grid --> Neighbors["Neighbor Detection"]
    
    Neighbors --> OptimizedCalc["Optimized ASA<br/>Calculation"]
    
    AllToAll["All-to-All O(n²)"] -.-> SpatialHash["Spatial Hash O(n)"]
    SpatialHash --> Performance["~4x Performance<br/>Improvement"]
```

**Spatial Hashing Optimization**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/asa/AsaCalculator.java:389-440](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/contact/Grid.java:59-516]()

## Interface Detection and Analysis

### StructureInterface Representation

The `StructureInterface` class represents contacts between two molecular chains, storing atom pairs, contact distances, and buried surface areas.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class StructureInterface {
        +Pair~Atom[]~ molecules
        +Pair~String~ moleculeIds
        +Pair~CrystalTransform~ transforms
        +AtomContactSet contacts
        +Map~ResidueNumber,GroupAsa~ groupAsas1
        +Map~ResidueNumber,GroupAsa~ groupAsas2
        +double totalArea
        +getTotalArea() double
        +getContactOverlapScore() double
        +isSymRelated() boolean
        +isHomomeric() boolean
    }
    
    class AtomContactSet {
        +List~AtomContact~ contacts
        +double cutoff
        +size() int
    }
    
    class GroupAsa {
        +Group group
        +double asaU
        +double asaC
        +getBsa() double
        +getBsaToAsaRatio() double
    }
    
    StructureInterface *-- AtomContactSet
    StructureInterface *-- GroupAsa
```

**StructureInterface Class Structure**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/contact/StructureInterface.java:62-819]()

### Interface Analysis Workflow

The interface analysis system provides multiple approaches for finding molecular interfaces, from simple contact detection to comprehensive crystal lattice analysis.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    StructInput["Structure Input"] --> Choice{Analysis Type}
    
    Choice -->|Simple| InterfaceFinder["InterfaceFinder"]
    Choice -->|Crystallographic| CrystalBuilder["CrystalBuilder"]
    
    InterfaceFinder --> BoundingBox["BoundingBox Overlap"]
    InterfaceFinder --> ContactCalc["Contact Calculation"]
    
    CrystalBuilder --> SpaceGroup["Space Group Operations"]
    CrystalBuilder --> CellExpansion["Unit Cell Expansion"]
    CrystalBuilder --> SymmetryCheck["Symmetry Redundancy Check"]
    
    ContactCalc --> StructInterfaceList["StructureInterfaceList"]
    SymmetryCheck --> StructInterfaceList
    
    StructInterfaceList --> AsaAnalysis["ASA Analysis"]
    StructInterfaceList --> Clustering["Interface Clustering"]
    
    AsaAnalysis --> BuriedArea["Buried Surface Area"]
    Clustering --> ContactOverlap["Contact Overlap Scoring"]
```

**Interface Analysis Workflow**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/contact/InterfaceFinder.java:22-107](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/xtal/CrystalBuilder.java:45-632]()

### Crystal Interface Analysis

The `CrystalBuilder` class performs comprehensive interface analysis by generating symmetry mates and detecting contacts across the crystal lattice.

| Parameter | Default Value | Description |
|-----------|---------------|-------------|
| `DEF_NUM_CELLS` | 20 | Number of neighboring cells to search |
| `DEFAULT_INTERFACE_DISTANCE_CUTOFF` | 5.5 Å | Maximum distance for interface contacts |
| `DEFAULT_CONTACT_OVERLAP_SCORE_CLUSTER_CUTOFF` | 0.2 | Threshold for interface clustering |

**Crystal Builder Configuration**

The system handles various crystallographic scenarios including non-standard space groups, missing unit cell information, and non-standard coordinate frames.

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/xtal/CrystalBuilder.java:65-71]()

## Contact Calculation and Spatial Data Structures

### Grid-Based Contact Detection

The `Grid` class implements spatial hashing for efficient contact calculation, dividing 3D space into cells of size equal to the cutoff distance.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Points["3D Coordinates"] --> GridHash["Grid Hash Function"]
    GridHash --> Cells["Grid Cells"]
    
    Cells --> CellContacts["Intra-Cell Contacts"]
    Cells --> NeighborContacts["Inter-Cell Contacts"]
    
    CellContacts --> ContactList["Contact List"]
    NeighborContacts --> ContactList
    
    subgraph "Grid Cell Structure"
        GridCell["GridCell"]
        IIndices["iIndices: List<Integer>"]
        JIndices["jIndices: List<Integer>"]
        GridCell --> IIndices
        GridCell --> JIndices
    end
```

**Grid-Based Spatial Hashing**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/contact/Grid.java:59-96](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/contact/GridCell.java:35-175]()

### BoundingBox Optimization

`BoundingBox` objects provide rapid overlap detection to avoid unnecessary contact calculations between distant molecular regions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    AtomCoords["Atom Coordinates"] --> BBCalc["BoundingBox Calculation"]
    BBCalc --> MinMax["Min/Max X,Y,Z"]
    
    MinMax --> OverlapTest["overlaps(cutoff)"]
    OverlapTest -->|True| DetailedCalc["Detailed Contact Calculation"]
    OverlapTest -->|False| Skip["Skip Calculation"]
    
    subgraph "Overlap Detection"
        XOverlap["X-dimension overlap"]
        YOverlap["Y-dimension overlap"] 
        ZOverlap["Z-dimension overlap"]
        XOverlap --> AllDims["All 3 dimensions<br/>must overlap"]
        YOverlap --> AllDims
        ZOverlap --> AllDims
    end
```

**BoundingBox Overlap Detection**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/contact/BoundingBox.java:42-255]()

## Interface Clustering and Classification

### Contact Overlap Scoring

The system uses Jaccard similarity (intersection over union) of contact sets to measure interface similarity and perform clustering.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Interface1["Interface A Contacts"] --> Jaccard["Jaccard Score Calculation"]
    Interface2["Interface B Contacts"] --> Jaccard
    
    Jaccard --> ScoreMatrix["Similarity Matrix"]
    ScoreMatrix --> SingleLinkage["Single Linkage Clustering"]
    SingleLinkage --> Clusters["Interface Clusters"]
    
    subgraph "Similarity Calculation"
        Intersection["Contact Set Intersection"]
        Union["Contact Set Union"]
        Score["Score = |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|"]
        Intersection --> Score
        Union --> Score
    end
```

**Interface Clustering Pipeline**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/contact/StructureInterfaceList.java:375-451]()

### Interface Classification

The system classifies interfaces based on several criteria:

| Classification | Method | Description |
|----------------|---------|-------------|
| Homomeric/Heteromeric | `isHomomeric()` | Same vs different entities |
| Symmetric/Asymmetric | `isSymRelated()` | Crystallographic symmetry |
| Isologous/Heterologous | `isIsologous()` | Self-contact overlap analysis |
| Infinite/Finite | `isInfinite()` | Crystal translation properties |

**Interface Classification Types**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/contact/StructureInterface.java:375-404]()

## Performance Considerations

The system implements several optimization strategies:

1. **Spatial Hashing**: Reduces neighbor finding from O(n²) to O(n)
2. **BoundingBox Pre-filtering**: Eliminates distant molecule pairs early
3. **Multi-threading**: Parallel ASA calculation with configurable thread count
4. **Sorted Neighbor Lists**: Optimizes occlusion checking in ASA calculation

The `DEFAULT_ASA_SPHERE_POINTS` of 3000 provides a balance between accuracy and performance for interface area calculations.

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/contact/StructureInterfaceList.java:62-67](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/asa/AsaCalculator.java:466-470]()

- [biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/TestSubunitExtractor.java](biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/TestSubunitExtractor.java)

</details>



This document covers BioJava's capabilities for analyzing protein quaternary structure through subunit clustering and alignment algorithms. The system provides tools for identifying equivalent subunits within protein complexes, determining stoichiometry, and aligning quaternary structures between different proteins.

For information about protein symmetry analysis, see [Protein Symmetry Analysis](#3.1). For surface area and interface analysis tools, see [Surface Area and Interface Analysis](#3.2).

## Overview

BioJava's quaternary structure analysis system operates through a multi-step process that extracts protein subunits from structures, clusters equivalent subunits using sequence and/or structural similarity, and enables comparative analysis of protein assemblies.

### Quaternary Structure Analysis Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Structure["Structure Object"] --> SubunitExtractor["SubunitExtractor"]
    SubunitExtractor --> Subunits["List<Subunit>"]
    Subunits --> SubunitClusterer["SubunitClusterer"]
    SubunitClusterer --> Clusters["List<SubunitCluster>"]
    Clusters --> Stoichiometry["Stoichiometry"]
    
    Clusters --> QuatSymmetryDetector["QuatSymmetryDetector"]
    QuatSymmetryDetector --> SymmetryResults["QuatSymmetryResults"]
    
    Subunits --> QsAlign["QsAlign Algorithm"]
    QsAlign --> QsAlignResult["QsAlignResult"]
    
    Clusters --> MultipleAlignment["MultipleAlignment"]
    
    subgraph "Clustering Methods"
        SeqMethod["SEQUENCE"]
        StructMethod["STRUCTURE"] 
        SeqStructMethod["SEQUENCE_STRUCTURE"]
    end
    
    SubunitClusterer -.-> SeqMethod
    SubunitClusterer -.-> StructMethod
    SubunitClusterer -.-> SeqStructMethod
```

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitExtractor.java:65-94](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitClusterer.java:50-136]()

## Core Components

### SubunitExtractor

The `SubunitExtractor` is responsible for converting protein chains from a `Structure` object into individual `Subunit` objects that can be analyzed for clustering.

**Key Features:**
- Extracts only protein chains from structures
- Applies length filtering with adaptive minimum sequence lengths
- Handles both asymmetric units and biological assemblies

The extractor uses adaptive length thresholds to accommodate structures with very short chains (such as collagen), adjusting the minimum sequence length based on the median chain length.

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitExtractor.java:65-143]()

### SubunitClusterer 

The `SubunitClusterer` implements the main clustering algorithm that groups equivalent subunits based on sequence and/or structural similarity.

#### Clustering Methods

| Method | Description | Use Case |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| `SEQUENCE` | Sequence-based clustering using pairwise alignments | High sequence identity subunits |
| `STRUCTURE` | Structure-based clustering using 3D alignment | Structurally similar but sequence-divergent subunits |
| `SEQUENCE_STRUCTURE` | Combined approach with both methods | Comprehensive analysis including pseudosymmetry detection |

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitClustererMethod.java:31-68]()

### SubunitCluster

The `SubunitCluster` class represents a group of equivalent subunits and provides methods for cluster manipulation and analysis.

#### Core SubunitCluster Operations

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class SubunitCluster {
        -List~Subunit~ subunits
        -List~List~Integer~~ subunitEQR
        -int representative
        -SubunitClustererMethod method
        -boolean pseudoStoichiometric
        +mergeIdentical(SubunitCluster other) boolean
        +mergeSequence(SubunitCluster other, params) boolean
        +mergeStructure(SubunitCluster other, params) boolean
        +divideInternally(params) boolean
        +getMultipleAlignment() MultipleAlignment
        +getAlignedAtomsSubunits() List~Atom[]~
    }
    
    class Subunit {
        -Atom[] representativeAtoms
        -String name
        -String identifier
        -Structure structure
        +getProteinSequence() ProteinSequence
        +size() int
    }
    
    class SubunitClustererParameters {
        -double sequenceIdentityThreshold
        -double rmsdThreshold
        -SubunitClustererMethod clustererMethod
        -boolean internalSymmetry
        -boolean useEntityIdForSeqIdentityDetermination
    }
    
    SubunitCluster --> Subunit
    SubunitCluster --> SubunitClustererParameters
```

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitCluster.java:77-854](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitClustererParameters.java:36-532]()

## Clustering Algorithm Details

### Sequence-Based Clustering

Sequence clustering uses pairwise sequence alignments with configurable identity and coverage thresholds. The algorithm supports both local and global alignment metrics.

**Default Thresholds:**
- High confidence sequence identity: 95% (local) / 85% (global)
- Sequence coverage: 75%

For performance optimization with large complexes, the system can use entity ID comparison to avoid expensive sequence alignments when subunits belong to the same molecular entity.

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitCluster.java:361-475](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitClustererParameters.java:48]()

### Structure-Based Clustering

Structure clustering performs 3D structural alignments using configurable structural alignment algorithms (default: CE-CP).

**Default Thresholds:**
- RMSD threshold: 3.0 Å
- Structure coverage: 75%
- TM-Score threshold: 0.5

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitCluster.java:491-581]()

### Internal Symmetry Detection

The clustering system can detect and split internally symmetric subunits into their symmetric repeats using the CE-Symm algorithm.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    InternalSubunit["Symmetric Subunit"] --> CeSymm["CE-Symm Analysis"]
    CeSymm --> MultipleRepeats["Multiple Symmetric Repeats"]
    MultipleRepeats --> NewClusters["Updated SubunitClusters"]
    
    CeSymm --> Parameters["Coverage & RMSD Thresholds"]
    Parameters --> Decision{"Significant Symmetry?"}
    Decision -->|Yes| Split["Split into Repeats"]
    Decision -->|No| Keep["Keep Original"]
```

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitCluster.java:643-746]()

## Stoichiometry Representation

The `Stoichiometry` class provides human-readable representation of protein assembly composition with flexible formatting strategies.

### Stoichiometry String Strategies

| Strategy | Description | Example |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `CYCLE` | Cycles through alphabet when clusters exceed letters | `A2B2C2...ZABC` |
| `DOUBLE` | Uses two-letter combinations for many clusters | `AA2AB2AC2...` |
| `QUESTIONMARK` | Uses '?' for excess clusters | `A2B2C2...Z???` |
| `CUSTOM` | User-defined string generation function | Custom format |

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/symmetry/core/Stoichiometry.java:39-366]()

## Quaternary Structure Alignment (QsAlign)

The `QsAlign` algorithm performs quaternary structure alignment between two protein complexes by matching equivalent subunits and calculating optimal superposition.

### QsAlign Algorithm Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input1["Structure 1"] --> Extract1["Extract Subunits"]
    Input2["Structure 2"] --> Extract2["Extract Subunits"]
    
    Extract1 --> Cluster1["Cluster Subunits"]
    Extract2 --> Cluster2["Cluster Subunits"]
    
    Cluster1 --> Match["Match SubunitClusters"]
    Cluster2 --> Match
    
    Match --> Align["Align Assemblies"]
    Align --> Evaluate["Evaluate Matches"]
    
    Evaluate --> Result["QsAlignResult"]
    
    subgraph "Matching Criteria"
        Centroid["Centroid Distance"]
        Orientation["Orientation Angle"]
        RMSD["RMSD Threshold"]
    end
    
    Align --> Centroid
    Align --> Orientation  
    Align --> RMSD
```

**Algorithm Parameters:**
- Maximum centroid distance: 10.0 Å
- Maximum orientation angle: π/6 radians (30°)
- Maximum RMSD: 10.0 Å

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/quaternary/QsAlign.java:67-378](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/quaternary/QsAlignParameters.java:30-95]()

### QsAlign Result Types

The algorithm classifies quaternary structure relationships into four categories:

| Relationship | Description |
|--------------|-------------|
| `EQUIVALENT` | All subunits from both structures are matched |
| `PARTIAL_COMPLETE` | All subunits from one structure are matched |
| `PARTIAL_INCOMPLETE` | Some subunits from both structures are matched |
| `DIFFERENT` | No subunit matches found |

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/quaternary/QsAlignResult.java:119-136]()

## Integration with Symmetry Analysis

The subunit clustering system integrates with BioJava's symmetry detection framework through the `QuatSymmetrySubunits` class, which adapts clustered subunits for symmetry analysis.

### QuatSymmetrySubunits Bridge

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class QuatSymmetrySubunits {
        -List~Point3d[]~ caCoords
        -List~Point3d~ centers
        -List~Integer~ clusterIds
        -List~SubunitCluster~ clusters
        -MomentsOfInertia momentsOfInertia
        +getFolds() List~Integer~
        +getCenters() List~Point3d~
        +getMomentsOfInertia() MomentsOfInertia
    }
    
    class SubunitCluster {
        +getAlignedAtomsSubunit(int) Atom[]
        +size() int
    }
    
    class QuatSymmetryDetector {
        +calcGlobalSymmetry(clusters, params) QuatSymmetryResults
        +calcLocalSymmetries(clusters, params) List~QuatSymmetryResults~
    }
    
    QuatSymmetrySubunits --> SubunitCluster
    QuatSymmetryDetector --> QuatSymmetrySubunits
```

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/symmetry/core/QuatSymmetrySubunits.java:47-287]()

## Usage Examples

### Basic Subunit Clustering

```java
// Extract and cluster subunits
Structure structure = StructureIO.getStructure("4hhb");
SubunitClustererParameters params = new SubunitClustererParameters();
params.setClustererMethod(SubunitClustererMethod.SEQUENCE);

Stoichiometry stoichiometry = SubunitClusterer.cluster(structure, params);
List<SubunitCluster> clusters = stoichiometry.getClusters();
```

### Quaternary Structure Alignment

```java
// Align two quaternary structures
Structure s1 = StructureIO.getStructure("1bcc");
Structure s2 = StructureIO.getStructure("1kb9");

SubunitClustererParameters clusterParams = new SubunitClustererParameters();
QsAlignParameters alignParams = new QsAlignParameters();

QsAlignResult result = QsAlign.align(s1, s2, clusterParams, alignParams);
```

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/demo/DemoQsAlign.java:48-67](), [biojava-integrationtest/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/test/symmetry/TestQuatSymmetryDetectorExamples.java:67-83]()

## Performance Considerations

For large protein complexes (e.g., viral capsids), the system provides optimization strategies:

1. **Entity ID-based clustering**: Bypasses sequence alignment for identical entities
2. **Structure-only mode**: Skips sequence clustering for speed
3. **Reduced precision alignment**: Uses non-optimized structural alignment

The entity ID optimization can reduce clustering time from hours to minutes for large complexes like viral capsids.

**Sources:** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/cluster/SubunitClusterer.java:74-80](), [biojava-integrationtest/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/test/symmetry/TestQuatSymmetryDetectorExamples.java:402-435]()

This document covers BioJava's framework for representing and computing multiple protein structure alignments. The system provides data structures to store alignment results, algorithms to generate alignments (particularly the Monte Carlo-based MultipleMC algorithm), and utilities for analysis and visualization. For pairwise structure alignment tools, see the Structure Alignment module. For sequence-based multiple alignments, see the Core Alignment module.

## Core Data Model

BioJava's multiple structure alignment system is built around a hierarchical data model that can represent flexible and non-topological alignments, including circular permutations.

### Hierarchy Overview

```mermaid
graph TD
    MAE["MultipleAlignmentEnsemble"] --> MA["MultipleAlignment"]
    MA --> BS["BlockSet"]
    BS --> B["Block"]
    
    MAE --> |"contains"| Structures["Structure Identifiers"]
    MAE --> |"contains"| Atoms["Atom Arrays"]
    MAE --> |"contains"| Metadata["Algorithm Metadata"]
    
    BS --> |"has"| Transform["Transformation Matrices"]
    B --> |"contains"| AlignRes["Aligned Residue Lists"]
    
    MA -.-> |"convenience access"| B
```

**Data Model Hierarchy**

The core interfaces define a four-level hierarchy where each level serves a specific purpose in representing complex structural alignments.

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/MultipleAlignmentEnsemble.java:1-231](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/MultipleAlignment.java:1-221](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/BlockSet.java:1-163](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/Block.java:1-179]()

### Key Interfaces and Implementations

| Interface | Implementation | Purpose |
|-----------|----------------|---------|
| `MultipleAlignmentEnsemble` | `MultipleAlignmentEnsembleImpl` | Top-level container holding structures and algorithm metadata |
| `MultipleAlignment` | `MultipleAlignmentImpl` | Single alignment result with multiple BlockSets |
| `BlockSet` | `BlockSetImpl` | Flexible alignment part with transformation matrices |
| `Block` | `BlockImpl` | Sequential aligned residues within a BlockSet |

The `ScoresCache` interface provides score storage across all levels, allowing algorithms to cache computed metrics like RMSD and TM-scores.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Core Interfaces"
        MAE[MultipleAlignmentEnsemble]
        MA[MultipleAlignment] 
        BS[BlockSet]
        B[Block]
        SC[ScoresCache]
    end
    
    subgraph "Implementations"
        MAEI[MultipleAlignmentEnsembleImpl]
        MAI[MultipleAlignmentImpl]
        BSI[BlockSetImpl] 
        BI[BlockImpl]
        ASC[AbstractScoresCache]
    end
    
    MAE -.-> MAEI
    MA -.-> MAI
    BS -.-> BSI
    B -.-> BI
    SC -.-> ASC
    
    MAEI --> ASC
    MAI --> ASC
    BSI --> ASC
    BI --> ASC
```

**Interface Implementation Relationships**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/MultipleAlignmentEnsembleImpl.java:1-402](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/MultipleAlignmentImpl.java:1-289](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/BlockSetImpl.java:1-246](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/BlockImpl.java:1-202]()

## Monte Carlo Multiple Alignment Algorithm

The MultipleMC algorithm is BioJava's primary tool for generating multiple structure alignments. It combines pairwise alignments into a seed alignment, then optimizes it using Monte Carlo methods.

### Algorithm Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["List of Atom Arrays"] --> Pairwise["Generate All Pairwise Alignments"]
    Pairwise --> |"AFPChain objects"| Reference["Choose Reference Structure"]
    Reference --> |"lowest average RMSD"| Combine["Combine Reference Alignments"]
    Combine --> |"MultipleAlignment seed"| MC["Monte Carlo Optimization"]
    
    subgraph "MC Optimization Loop"
        MC --> Move["Random Move Operation"]
        Move --> |"40%"| Shift["Shift Row"]
        Move --> |"30%"| Expand["Expand Block"] 
        Move --> |"15%"| Shrink["Shrink Block"]
        Move --> |"15%"| Gap["Insert Gap"]
        
        Shift --> Score["Calculate MC Score"]
        Expand --> Score
        Shrink --> Score
        Gap --> Score
        
        Score --> Accept{"Accept Move?"}
        Accept --> |"if score improves or probability"| Update["Update Alignment"]
        Accept --> |"reject"| Revert["Revert to Previous"]
        Update --> Check{"Converged?"}
        Revert --> Check
        Check --> |"no"| Move
    end
    
    Check --> |"yes"| Final["Final Superposition & Scoring"]
    Final --> Result["Optimized MultipleAlignment"]
```

**MultipleMC Algorithm Flow**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/mc/MultipleMcMain.java:120-172](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/mc/MultipleMcOptimizer.java:239-335]()

### Core Algorithm Classes

The MultipleMC algorithm is implemented across several key classes:

- `MultipleMcMain`: Main algorithm entry point implementing `MultipleStructureAligner`
- `MultipleMcOptimizer`: Monte Carlo optimization engine implementing `Callable<MultipleAlignment>`
- `MultipleMcParameters`: Configuration parameters for the algorithm

The optimization process uses four types of moves to modify alignments:

1. **Shift Row** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/mc/MultipleMcOptimizer.java:454-647](): Shifts aligned residues left or right within a structure
2. **Expand Block** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/mc/MultipleMcOptimizer.java:656-771](): Adds new columns to alignment blocks
3. **Shrink Block** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/mc/MultipleMcOptimizer.java:776-818](): Removes alignment columns with high average distance
4. **Insert Gap** [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/mc/MultipleMcOptimizer.java:400-442](): Introduces gaps at positions with high structural deviation

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/mc/MultipleMcMain.java:1-429](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/mc/MultipleMcOptimizer.java:1-854](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/mc/MultipleMcParameters.java:1-225]()

## Alignment Tools and Utilities

The `MultipleAlignmentTools` class provides essential utilities for working with multiple alignments, from sequence generation to phylogenetic analysis.

### Core Utility Functions

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Sequence Operations"
        SAL["getSequenceAlignment()"] --> |"with gaps"| FullSeq["Full Sequence Alignment"]
        BSA["getBlockSequenceAlignment()"] --> |"blocks only"| BlockSeq["Block-based Alignment"]
        MSA["toProteinMSA()"] --> |"convert to"| ProtMSA["MultipleSequenceAlignment"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structural Analysis"
        TA["transformAtoms()"] --> TransAtoms["Superimposed Atom Arrays"]
        ARD["getAverageResidueDistances()"] --> DistMatrix["Distance Matrix"]
        RMSD["getRMSDMatrix()"] --> RMSDMat["RMSD Matrix"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phylogenetic Analysis"  
        KT["getKimuraTree()"] --> |"sequence-based"| SeqTree["Phylogenetic Tree"]
        HT["getHSDMTree()"] --> |"structure-aware"| StrucTree["Structure-derived Tree"]
        ST["getStructuralTree()"] --> |"RMSD-based"| RMSDTree["Distance Tree"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Format Conversion"
        MS["toMultimodelStructure()"] --> MMStruct["Multi-model Structure"]
        AS["getAlignedStructure()"] --> AlignStruct["Aligned Structure"]
        ER["getEquivalentResidues()"] --> ResMatrix["Residue Matrix"]
    end
```

**MultipleAlignmentTools Function Categories**

### Sequence Alignment Generation

The tools provide two main approaches for generating sequence alignments from structural alignments:

- `getSequenceAlignment()` [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/MultipleAlignmentTools.java:108-298](): Includes all residues with aligned positions in uppercase and unaligned in lowercase
- `getBlockSequenceAlignment()` [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/MultipleAlignmentTools.java:346-451](): Shows only residues within alignment blocks

Both methods return position mappings between sequence and structure coordinates for GUI applications.

### Structural Transformations

The `transformAtoms()` method [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/MultipleAlignmentTools.java:659-721]() applies the stored transformation matrices to create superimposed atom arrays. This enables:

- RMSD calculations across all structure pairs
- Visualization of aligned structures
- Distance-based scoring functions

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/MultipleAlignmentTools.java:1-1010]()

## Superposition Algorithms

BioJava provides multiple algorithms for superimposing structures in multiple alignments, each with different strategies for handling gaps and reference structures.

### Superimposer Implementations

```mermaid
graph TD
    MS[MultipleSuperimposer] --> RS[ReferenceSuperimposer]
    MS --> CS[CoreSuperimposer]
    
    RS --> |"superimposes"| AllRes["All Aligned Residues"]
    CS --> |"superimposes"| CoreRes["Core Residues Only"]
    
    subgraph "Reference Strategy"
        RS --> RefCalc["Calculate vs Reference Structure"]
        RefCalc --> RefTrans["Generate Transformation Matrices"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Strategy" 
        CS --> CoreCalc["Calculate Core Positions"]
        CoreCalc --> CoreTrans["Core-based Transformations"]
        CoreCalc --> |"eliminates"| GapCols["Gapped Columns"]
    end
```

**Superposition Algorithm Comparison**

| Algorithm | Strategy | Handles Gaps | Use Case |
|-----------|----------|--------------|----------|
| `ReferenceSuperimposer` | All residues vs reference | Skips null positions | General alignment display |
| `CoreSuperimposer` | Core residues only | Excludes gapped columns | Conservative superposition |

Both algorithms implement the `MultipleSuperimposer` interface and use SVD-based superposition via `SuperPositions.superpose()`.

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/ReferenceSuperimposer.java:1-163](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/CoreSuperimposer.java:1-174](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/MultipleSuperimposer.java:1-66]()

## Scoring and Analysis

The `MultipleAlignmentScorer` class provides comprehensive scoring functions for evaluating alignment quality and structural similarity.

### Scoring Functions

| Score Type | Method | Description |
|------------|--------|-------------|
| RMSD | `getRMSD()` | All-pairs root mean square deviation |
| Ref-RMSD | `getRefRMSD()` | Average RMSD to reference structure |
| TM-Score | `getAvgTMScore()` | Average template modeling score |
| MC-Score | `getMCScore()` | Monte Carlo optimization objective function |

The MC-Score [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/MultipleAlignmentScorer.java:321-400]() combines geometric quality with gap penalties:

```
MC-Score = Σ(aligned_residues) - gap_open_penalty * gaps - gap_extend_penalty * gap_length - distance_penalty * avg_distance
```

### Output Formats

The `MultipleAlignmentWriter` class supports multiple output formats:

- **FASTA**: Sequence alignment format
- **FatCat**: Detailed alignment with block information  
- **Aligned Residues**: Tab-delimited residue positions
- **XML**: Complete alignment serialization
- **3D Format**: I-TASSER template-target format

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/MultipleAlignmentScorer.java:1-447](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/multiple/util/MultipleAlignmentWriter.java:1-377]()

## Usage Example

The following demonstrates basic usage of the MultipleMC algorithm:

```java
// Load structures
AtomCache cache = new AtomCache();
List<Atom[]> atomArrays = new ArrayList<>();
List<StructureIdentifier> ids = new ArrayList<>();

for (String name : structureNames) {
    StructureIdentifier id = new StructureName(name);
    ids.add(id);
    atomArrays.add(cache.getAtoms(id));
}

// Configure algorithm
MultipleMcMain algorithm = new MultipleMcMain(new CeMain());
MultipleMcParameters params = (MultipleMcParameters) algorithm.getParameters();
params.setMinBlockLen(10);
params.setGapExtension(20.0);

// Generate alignment
MultipleAlignment result = algorithm.align(atomArrays);
result.getEnsemble().setStructureIdentifiers(ids);

// Output results
System.out.println(MultipleAlignmentWriter.toFatCat(result));
```

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/demo/DemoMultipleMC.java:94-124](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/demo/DemoMultipleMC.java:94-122]()

This page documents BioJava's specialized analysis modules that provide domain-specific computational tools for genomics and nucleic acid structural analysis. These modules extend beyond the core data structures and file format support to offer advanced analytical capabilities for biological sequence analysis.

The specialized analysis modules are organized into two main categories: genomic analysis tools for working with chromosomal coordinates and coding sequences, and nucleic acid structure analysis tools for calculating base pair parameters and structural properties. For detailed information about protein structure analysis tools, see [Structural Analysis Tools](#3). For basic sequence alignment algorithms, see [Core Architecture](#2).

## Module Architecture Overview

The specialized analysis modules build upon BioJava's core data structures to provide advanced analytical capabilities:

## Genomic Analysis Tools

The genomic analysis module provides sophisticated tools for working with chromosomal coordinates, coding sequences, and genomic feature mapping. The primary entry point is the `ChromosomeMappingTools` class, which handles bidirectional coordinate transformations between genomic and coding sequence positions.

## Nucleic Acid Structure Analysis

The nucleic acid structure analysis module implements the el Hassan-Calladine method for calculating base pair and base-pair step parameters in nucleic acid structures. The analysis supports both DNA and RNA structures with multiple specialized implementations for different analysis scenarios.

### Base Pair Parameter Analysis

The `BasePairParameters` class serves as the foundation for nucleic acid structural analysis:

```mermaid
    end
    
    subgraph "Specialized Implementations"
```

The analysis workflow processes nucleic acid structures through several key stages:

| Analysis Stage | Method | Function |
|----------------|--------|----------|

| Base pair detection | `findPairs()` | Locates Watson-Crick and other base pairs |
| Reference frame calculation | `basePairReferenceFrame()` | Establishes coordinate system for each pair |
| Parameter calculation | `calculateTp()` | Computes geometric parameters |

### Specialized Analysis Implementations

The module provides specialized implementations for different analysis scenarios:

**TertiaryBasePairParameters**: Designed for RNA tertiary structure analysis, this implementation relaxes the standard constraints to detect intra-strand base pairs and non-canonical interactions. It uses configurable thresholds for stagger (`maxStagger`) and propeller twist (`maxPropeller`) parameters.

**MismatchedBasePairParameters**: Focuses on inter-strand base pairs that may not follow canonical Watson-Crick pairing rules. This implementation adds additional filtering parameters including maximum shear (`maxShear`) and stretch (`maxStretch`) values to identify structurally valid but non-canonical base pairs.

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/TertiaryBasePairParameters.java:47-51](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/MismatchedBasePairParameters.java:52-55]()

For detailed information about base pair parameter calculations and nucleic acid structural analysis algorithms, see [Nucleic Acid Structure Analysis](#4.2).

## Purpose and Scope

This document covers BioJava's genomic analysis and chromosome mapping capabilities, which provide tools for working with genomic coordinates, gene structures, and coding sequence (CDS) analysis. The primary functionality enables conversion between chromosomal positions and mRNA coordinates, extraction of exon boundaries, CDS length calculations, and retrieval of genomic sequences.

For nucleic acid structure analysis including base pair parameters, see [Nucleic Acid Structure Analysis](#4.2). For general sequence handling and file format support, see [File Format Support and Parsing](#2.2).

## System Architecture

The genomic analysis system is built around coordinate transformation between different genomic reference frames:


**Sources:** [biojava-genome/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/genome/util/ChromosomeMappingTools.java:210-224](), [biojava-genome/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/genome/util/ChromosomeMappingTools.java:548-569](), [biojava-genome/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/genome/util/ChromosomeMappingTools.java:501-537]()

### Exon Range Extraction

The `getCDSExonRanges()` and `getChromosomalRangesForCDS()` methods extract exon boundaries in different coordinate systems:

| Method | Coordinate System | Use Case |
|--------|------------------|----------|
| `getCDSExonRanges()` | CDS coordinates | Protein domain mapping |
| `getChromosomalRangesForCDS()` | Genomic coordinates | Variant annotation |

**Sources:** [biojava-genome/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/genome/util/ChromosomeMappingTools.java:577-581](), [biojava-genome/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/genome/util/ChromosomeMappingTools.java:588-592]()

## Sequence Extraction and Translation

### DNA Sequence Extraction

The system integrates with `TwoBitFacade` to extract genomic sequences:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant CMT as "ChromosomeMappingTools"
    participant TBF as "TwoBitFacade"
    participant PMT as "ProteinMappingTools"
    
    Client->>CMT: getTranscriptDNASequence(twoBitFacade, gcp)
    CMT->>CMT: getCDSRegions(exonStarts, exonEnds, cdsStart, cdsEnd)
    
    loop For each CDS region
        CMT->>TBF: getSequence(chromosome, start, end)
        TBF-->>CMT: DNA sequence fragment
    end
    
    CMT->>CMT: Concatenate fragments
    
    alt Reverse strand
        CMT->>CMT: Reverse complement sequence
    end
    
    CMT-->>Client: DNASequence
    
    opt Protein translation
        Client->>PMT: convertDNAtoProteinSequence(dnaSequence)
        PMT-->>Client: ProteinSequence
    end
```

**Sources:** [biojava-genome/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/genome/util/ChromosomeMappingTools.java:939-971](), [biojava-genome/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/genome/parsers/twobit/TwoBitFacade.java:81-85](), [biojava-genome/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/genome/util/ProteinMappingTools.java:36-50]()

### Coordinate System Configuration

The system supports configurable coordinate systems through `setCoordinateSystem()`:

```java
// Set to 0-based coordinates (default)
ChromosomeMappingTools.setCoordinateSystem(0);

// Set to 1-based coordinates
ChromosomeMappingTools.setCoordinateSystem(1);
```

**Sources:** [biojava-genome/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/genome/util/ChromosomeMappingTools.java:52-55]()

## Integration with BioJava Core

The genomic analysis module integrates with BioJava's core sequence handling:

- Uses `DNASequence` from `biojava-core` for sequence representation
- Leverages `Range<Integer>` from Google Guava for coordinate ranges
- Integrates with `ProteinSequence` for translation workflows

# Page: Nucleic Acid Structure Analysis

# Nucleic Acid Structure Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [biojava-alignment/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/alignment/NeedlemanWunschTest.java](biojava-alignment/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/alignment/NeedlemanWunschTest.java)
- [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/JmolTools.java](biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/JmolTools.java)
- [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java](biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java)
- [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/MismatchedBasePairParameters.java](biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/MismatchedBasePairParameters.java)
- [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/TertiaryBasePairParameters.java](biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/TertiaryBasePairParameters.java)
- [biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/TestBasePairParameters.java](biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/TestBasePairParameters.java)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document covers BioJava's nucleic acid structure analysis capabilities, specifically the calculation of base pair and base-pair step parameters for DNA and RNA structures. The system implements the el Hassan-Calladine method for characterizing nucleic acid geometry through systematic measurement of structural parameters between base pairs and consecutive base pair steps.

For genomic sequence analysis and chromosome mapping, see [Genomic Analysis and Chromosome Mapping](#4.1). For general structure visualization capabilities, see [Jmol Integration and Structure Visualization](#5.1).

## Base Pair Parameter Analysis System

BioJava provides a comprehensive framework for analyzing nucleic acid structural parameters based on the methodology described in Hassan & Calladine (2001). The system calculates both intra-base-pair parameters (buckle, propeller, opening, shear, stretch, stagger) and inter-base-pair step parameters (tilt, roll, twist, shift, slide, rise) for double-helical regions within protein-nucleic acid complexes or standalone nucleic acid structures.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Structures"
        PDB["PDB/mmCIF Structure"]
        Chains["Nucleic Acid Chains"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis Classes"
        BasePair["BasePairParameters"]
        Tertiary["TertiaryBasePairParameters"] 
        Mismatched["MismatchedBasePairParameters"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Standard Bases"
        BaseMap["BASE_MAP"]
        RingMap["RING_MAP"]
        Standards["STANDARD_BASES[]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Parameters"
        PairParams["Pairing Parameters<br/>buckle, propeller, opening<br/>shear, stretch, stagger"]
        StepParams["Step Parameters<br/>tilt, roll, twist<br/>shift, slide, rise"]
        RefFrames["Reference Frames"]
    end
    
    PDB --> Chains
    Chains --> BasePair
    BasePair --> Tertiary
    BasePair --> Mismatched
    
    BaseMap --> BasePair
    RingMap --> BasePair  
    Standards --> BasePair
    
    BasePair --> PairParams
    BasePair --> StepParams
    BasePair --> RefFrames
```

**Base Pair Parameter Analysis Architecture**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java:54-70]()

## Core Classes and Relationships

The nucleic acid analysis system centers around three main classes that provide different levels of base pair detection and analysis:

| Class | Purpose | Base Pair Detection |
|-------|---------|-------------------|
| `BasePairParameters` | Standard Watson-Crick pairs between separate strands | Canonical pairs with sequence alignment |
| `TertiaryBasePairParameters` | RNA tertiary structure analysis | Intra-strand and non-canonical pairs |
| `MismatchedBasePairParameters` | Non-canonical inter-strand pairs | Relaxed geometric criteria |

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class BasePairParameters {
        +Structure structure
        +boolean canonical
        +boolean useRNA
        +double[][] pairingParameters
        +double[][] stepParameters
        +List~String~ pairingNames
        +analyze() BasePairParameters
        +findPairs(chains) List~Pair~Group~~
        +basePairReferenceFrame(pair) Matrix4d
        +getBuckle(bp) Double
        +getPropeller(bp) Double
        +getTilt(bp) Double
        +getRoll(bp) Double
    }
    
    class TertiaryBasePairParameters {
        +double maxStagger
        +double maxPropeller
        +findPairs(chains) List~Pair~Group~~
        +setMaxStagger(double)
        +setMaxPropeller(double)
    }
    
    class MismatchedBasePairParameters {
        +double maxStagger
        +double maxShear
        +double maxStretch
        +double maxPropeller
        +findPairs(chains) List~Pair~Group~~
        +setMaxStagger(double)
        +setMaxShear(double)
    }
    
    BasePairParameters <|-- TertiaryBasePairParameters
    BasePairParameters <|-- MismatchedBasePairParameters
```

**Base Pair Parameter Class Hierarchy**

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java:71](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/TertiaryBasePairParameters.java:43](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/MismatchedBasePairParameters.java:42]()

## Standard Base Definitions and Coordinate System

The system uses hard-coded standard base geometries for adenine, guanine, thymine/uracil, and cytosine to establish reference coordinate systems. These standard bases are defined as PDB-format strings with idealized atomic coordinates.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Base Type Mapping"
        BaseMap["BASE_MAP<br/>DA/ADE/A → 0<br/>DG/GUA/G → 1<br/>DT/THY/T/U/URA → 2<br/>DC/CYT/C → 3"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Ring Atom Definitions"  
        RingMapPurine["Purines (A,G)<br/>C8,C2,N3,C4,C5,C6,N7,N1,N9"]
        RingMapPyrimidine["Pyrimidines (T/U,C)<br/>C6,C2,N3,C4,C5,N1"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Standard Coordinates"
        StandardA["Standard A<br/>ATOM N9 -1.291 4.498 0.000<br/>ATOM C8 0.024 4.897 0.000<br/>..."]
        StandardG["Standard G"]
        StandardT["Standard T/U"] 
        StandardC["Standard C"]
    end
    
    BaseMap --> RingMapPurine
    BaseMap --> RingMapPyrimidine
    RingMapPurine --> StandardA
    RingMapPurine --> StandardG
    RingMapPyrimidine --> StandardT
    RingMapPyrimidine --> StandardC
```

**Standard Base Reference System**

The `BASE_MAP` associates various PDB residue names with numerical base types, while `RING_MAP` defines the ring atoms used for superposition and parameter calculation. The `STANDARD_BASES` array contains idealized coordinates for each base type.

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java:128-146](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java:79-125]()

## Parameter Calculation Workflow

The analysis workflow follows a systematic process of structure parsing, base pair identification, and geometric parameter calculation:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["analyze()"] --> GetChains["getNucleicChains(nonredundant)"]
    GetChains --> FindPairs["findPairs(chains)"]
    FindPairs --> InitArrays["Initialize pairingParameters[][]<br/>stepParameters[][]"]
    
    InitArrays --> LoopStart["For each base pair i"]
    LoopStart --> CalcFrame["basePairReferenceFrame(pair)"]
    CalcFrame --> StorePair["Store pairing parameters<br/>pairParameters[0-5]"]
    
    StorePair --> CheckStep{i > 0?}
    CheckStep -->|Yes| CalcStep["Calculate step transform<br/>lastStep.invert()<br/>lastStep.mul(currentStep)"]
    CheckStep -->|No| NextPair["i++"]
    
    CalcStep --> StoreStep["calculateTp(transform)<br/>Store step parameters"]
    StoreStep --> NextPair
    
    NextPair --> MorePairs{More pairs?}
    MorePairs -->|Yes| LoopStart
    MorePairs -->|No| Return["Return this"]
```

**Parameter Calculation Flow**

The `basePairReferenceFrame` method performs superposition of actual base pairs onto standard base geometries using the `SuperPositionQCP` algorithm, establishing a local coordinate system for each base pair. Step parameters are calculated by comparing consecutive base pair reference frames.

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java:215-240](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java:533-627]()

## Specialized Analysis Implementations

### TertiaryBasePairParameters

The `TertiaryBasePairParameters` class extends the base functionality to detect intra-strand base pairs commonly found in RNA tertiary structures. It uses geometric criteria rather than sequence complementarity:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "TertiaryBasePairParameters.findPairs()"
        Start["For each chain"] --> SeqLoop["For each position j"]
        SeqLoop --> BackLoop["For k = length-1 to j+3"]
        BackLoop --> C1Check["Check C1'-C1' distance<br/>~10Å ± 4Å"]
        C1Check --> FrameCalc["Calculate reference frame"]
        FrameCalc --> StaggerTest["abs(stagger) < maxStagger"]
        StaggerTest --> PropTest["abs(propeller) < maxPropeller"]
        PropTest --> AddPair["Add to result"]
        AddPair --> FoundCheck{Found pair?}
        FoundCheck -->|No| BackLoop
        FoundCheck -->|Yes| NextJ["j++"]
        NextJ --> MoreJ{More positions?}
        MoreJ -->|Yes| SeqLoop
        MoreJ -->|No| CallSuper["Add super.findPairs()"]
    end
```

**Tertiary Structure Base Pair Detection**

Default thresholds: `maxStagger = 2.0 Å`, `maxPropeller = 60.0°`

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/TertiaryBasePairParameters.java:64-109]()

### MismatchedBasePairParameters  

The `MismatchedBasePairParameters` class identifies inter-strand pairs that don't follow Watson-Crick complementarity rules, using expanded geometric tolerance criteria:

| Parameter | Default Threshold | Purpose |
|-----------|------------------|---------|
| `maxStagger` | 2.0 Å | Vertical displacement limit |
| `maxShear` | 5.0 Å | Horizontal displacement limit |
| `maxStretch` | 5.0 Å | Distance variation limit |
| `maxPropeller` | 60.0° | Twist angle limit |

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/MismatchedBasePairParameters.java:46-55](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/MismatchedBasePairParameters.java:77-131]()

## Parameter Types and Accessor Methods

The system calculates twelve structural parameters organized into two categories:

### Pairing Parameters (intra-base-pair)
- **Angular parameters (degrees)**: `getBuckle()`, `getPropeller()`, `getOpening()`  
- **Translational parameters (Å)**: `getShear()`, `getStretch()`, `getStagger()`

### Step Parameters (inter-base-pair)
- **Angular parameters (degrees)**: `getTilt()`, `getRoll()`, `getTwist()`
- **Translational parameters (Å)**: `getShift()`, `getSlide()`, `getRise()`

The `calculateTp` method implements the mathematical transformation from 4×4 matrices to parameter space using trigonometric relationships defined in the el Hassan-Calladine methodology.

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java:307-425](), [biojava-structure/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/BasePairParameters.java:655-697]()

## Usage Examples

### Basic DNA Analysis
```java
Structure structure = StructureIO.getStructure("1KX5");
BasePairParameters bp = new BasePairParameters(structure);
bp.analyze();

// Access individual parameters
double buckle = bp.getBuckle(0);    // First base pair buckle
double twist = bp.getTwist(1);      // Second base pair step twist
```

### RNA Tertiary Structure Analysis  
```java
Structure structure = StructureIO.getStructure("3PHP");
TertiaryBasePairParameters bp = new TertiaryBasePairParameters(structure, true, false);
bp.setMaxStagger(2.5);  // Adjust tolerance
bp.analyze();
```

### Non-canonical Base Pair Detection
```java
MismatchedBasePairParameters bp = new MismatchedBasePairParameters(structure, false, false, false);
bp.setMaxShear(6.0);    // Allow more geometric variation
bp.analyze();
```

Sources: [biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/TestBasePairParameters.java:47-75](), [biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/basepairs/TestBasePairParameters.java:98-101]()

This document covers BioJava's graphical user interface components and visualization capabilities for structural biology data. The framework provides interactive 3D structure visualization through Jmol integration, 2D alignment panels for sequence and structural alignments, and comprehensive menu systems for user interaction. 

For information about the underlying structural analysis algorithms that these interfaces display, see [Structural Analysis Tools](#3). For details about the data models and file formats being visualized, see [Core Architecture](#2).

## Purpose and Scope

BioJava's visualization system enables interactive exploration of protein structures, structural alignments, and multiple sequence alignments through sophisticated graphical interfaces. The system supports both embedded components for integration into larger applications and standalone GUI applications for end-users.

## Core GUI Architecture

The visualization system is built around a modular architecture with distinct layers for different types of content display:

## Jmol Integration Framework

BioJava provides comprehensive 3D structure visualization through integration with the Jmol molecular viewer. The integration supports both pairwise and multiple structure alignments with coordinated highlighting and interactive selection.

The `JmolPanel` class serves as the core integration point with the Jmol viewer, handling structure loading, script execution, and user interaction events. It supports multiple input formats including PDB, mmCIF, and MMTF through BioJava's structure parsing system.

### Structure Alignment Visualization

The system provides specialized viewers for different types of structural alignments:

| Component | Purpose | Key Features |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| `StructureAlignmentJmol` | Pairwise structure alignments | Color coding by alignment blocks, zoom controls, selection highlighting |
| `MultipleAlignmentJmol` | Multiple structure alignments | Structure selection checkboxes, block-based coloring, phylogenetic tree display |
| `AbstractAlignmentJmol` | Base functionality | Mouse interaction, structure loading, menu integration |

The alignment viewers generate Jmol scripts dynamically to highlight aligned regions using coordinated color schemes. For pairwise alignments, the `getJmolString` method in `StructureAlignmentJmol` creates scripts that color equivalent residues with consistent colors across both structures [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/StructureAlignmentJmol.java:417-488]().

For multiple alignments, the coloring system supports both structure-based and block-based schemes, with the ability to toggle between different visualization modes through the interface controls [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/MultipleAlignmentJmol.java:419-465]().

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/StructureAlignmentJmol.java:417-632](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/MultipleAlignmentJmol.java:419-572]()

## 2D Alignment Panel System

BioJava provides interactive 2D sequence alignment panels that work in coordination with the 3D Jmol viewers. These panels display sequence alignments with position-specific coloring and support mouse-based selection of alignment regions.

```mermaid
    end

        ColorSchemes["Color schemes<br/>Similarity, blocks, structure"]
        SelectionHighlight["Selection highlighting"]
        PositionLabels["Residue position labels"]
    end
    
    AligPanel --> AFPCoordManager
    MultiplePanel --> MultipleCoordManager

    SelectionEvents --> AlignmentPositionListener

```

The alignment panels provide several key interaction modes:

- **Mouse hover**: Highlights corresponding positions in both 2D panel and 3D viewer
- **Click selection**: Selects individual alignment positions
- **Drag selection**: Selects ranges of alignment positions  
- **Keyboard modifiers**: Allows additive selection with Shift/Ctrl keys

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/aligpanel/AligPanel.java:1-501](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/aligpanel/MultipleAligPanel.java:1-501]()

### Coordinate Management System

The coordinate management system handles the complex mapping between different coordinate spaces:

| Coordinate Space | Manager Class | Purpose |
|------------------|---------------|---------|
| Panel coordinates | `AFPChainCoordManager` | Maps mouse positions to alignment positions for pairwise alignments |
| Sequence coordinates | `MultipleAlignmentCoordManager` | Maps positions for multiple sequence alignments |
| Structure coordinates | Position mapping methods | Links alignment positions to 3D structure atoms |

The coordinate managers implement methods like `getSeqPos()` and `getPanelPos()` to convert between pixel coordinates on the panel and logical alignment positions [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/aligpanel/AFPChainCoordManager.java:98-146]().

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/aligpanel/AFPChainCoordManager.java:98-216]()

|-----------|----------|----------|

## Standalone Protein Comparison Tool

BioJava includes a standalone GUI application for protein structure comparison, packaged as an executable JAR with all dependencies included.

### Application Structure

The protein comparison tool is configured as a Maven project that creates a shaded JAR containing:

- All BioJava modules (`biojava-core`, `biojava-structure`, `biojava-structure-gui`, `biojava-alignment`)
- Jmol viewer library (version 13.0.14)
- Logging frameworks (SLF4J, Log4j2)

The main class is specified as `org.biojava.nbio.structure.align.gui.AlignmentGui` in the JAR manifest [biojava-protein-comparison-tool/pom.xml:135]().

### Tool Capabilities

The standalone application provides:

| Feature | Implementation | Description |
|---------|----------------|-------------|
| Structure Loading | File picker dialogs | Load structures from local PDB files or fetch by ID |
| Alignment Algorithms | Algorithm selection | Choose from CE, FATCAT, and other alignment methods |
| 3D Visualization | Embedded Jmol viewer | Interactive 3D structure display with alignment highlighting |
| 2D Alignment View | Integrated alignment panels | Sequence-level view with position selection |
| Export Options | Multiple formats | Save alignments as XML, text, or image formats |

The application integrates all the visualization components described above into a cohesive user interface for structural biology analysis workflows.

Sources: [biojava-protein-comparison-tool/pom.xml:1-192]()

# Page: Jmol Integration and Structure Visualization

# Jmol Integration and Structure Visualization

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

This page documents BioJava's 3D structure visualization capabilities through Jmol integration, interactive alignment displays, and the coordination between 2D sequence alignments and 3D structural representations. The system provides comprehensive tools for visualizing both pairwise and multiple structure alignments with rich interactive features.

For information about the underlying structure alignment algorithms, see [3.4](#3.4). For details about alignment data models, see [2.1](#2.1).

## Core Architecture

The Jmol integration system is built around a hierarchy of visualization components that coordinate 3D structure display with 2D alignment representations. The architecture separates concerns between structure visualization, alignment display, and user interaction management.

### Class Hierarchy and Component Relationships

```mermaid
graph TD
    AbstractAlignmentJmol["AbstractAlignmentJmol<br/>Base visualization class"]

    MultipleAlignmentJmol["MultipleAlignmentJmol<br/>Multiple alignments"]
    
    JmolPanel["JmolPanel<br/>Core 3D viewer"]
    AligPanel["AligPanel<br/>Pairwise alignment display"]
    MultipleAligPanel["MultipleAligPanel<br/>Multiple alignment display"]
    
    MenuCreator["MenuCreator<br/>Menu system"]
    DisplayAFP["DisplayAFP<br/>Alignment utilities"]
    
    AbstractAlignmentJmol --> StructureAlignmentJmol
    AbstractAlignmentJmol --> MultipleAlignmentJmol
    
    AbstractAlignmentJmol --> JmolPanel
    StructureAlignmentJmol --> AligPanel
    MultipleAlignmentJmol --> MultipleAligPanel
    
    StructureAlignmentJmol --> MenuCreator
    MultipleAlignmentJmol --> MenuCreator
    StructureAlignmentJmol --> DisplayAFP
    
    JmolPanel --> MyJmolStatusListener["MyJmolStatusListener<br/>Status handling"]
```

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/AbstractAlignmentJmol.java:55-56](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/StructureAlignmentJmol.java:59](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/MultipleAlignmentJmol.java:75]()

### Data Flow and Visualization Pipeline

```mermaid

    AFPChain["AFPChain<br/>Pairwise alignment data"]
```

## Main Visualization Components

### AbstractAlignmentJmol Base Class

The `AbstractAlignmentJmol` class provides the foundation for all Jmol-based visualizations in BioJava. It manages the core `JmolPanel`, handles mouse interactions, and defines the interface for alignment-specific visualization logic.

| Method | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `setStructure(Structure)` | Load structure into Jmol viewer |
| `evalString(String)` | Execute Jmol scripting commands |
| `resetDisplay()` | Abstract method for resetting visualization |
| `initCoords()` | Abstract method for initializing coordinates |
| `destroy()` | Cleanup resources and listeners |

The base class implements mouse motion handling to provide atom information display and selection capabilities across all visualization types.

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/AbstractAlignmentJmol.java:55-97](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/AbstractAlignmentJmol.java:152-181]()

### StructureAlignmentJmol for Pairwise Alignments

`StructureAlignmentJmol` specializes the base class for pairwise structure alignments using `AFPChain` objects. It creates artificial two-model structures where aligned regions are colored distinctively.

Key visualization features:
- **Color Coding**: Orange and cyan coloring for aligned regions
- **Block Visualization**: Multi-block alignments use color gradients
- **Interactive Controls**: Zoom slider, spin control, style selection
- **Selection Display**: Click-to-select atom regions

```mermaid
graph LR
    AFPChain_Input["AFPChain"] --> getJmolString["getJmolString()"]
    ca1["Atom[] ca1"] --> getJmolString
    ca2["Atom[] ca2"] --> getJmolString
    
    getJmolString --> Script["Jmol Script<br/>Color commands"]
    Script --> JmolPanel_Exec["JmolPanel.evalString()"]
    
    getJmolString --> getMultiBlockJmolScript["getMultiBlockJmolScript()<br/>Multi-block coloring"]
    getMultiBlockJmolScript --> ColorUtils["ColorUtils<br/>Block color gradients"]
```

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/StructureAlignmentJmol.java:417-488](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/StructureAlignmentJmol.java:516-540]()

### MultipleAlignmentJmol for Multiple Structure Alignments

`MultipleAlignmentJmol` handles visualization of multiple structure alignments, supporting both structure-based and block-based coloring schemes. It includes additional controls for structure selection and block coloring.

Enhanced features for multiple alignments:
- **Structure Selection**: Individual structure visibility controls
- **Block Coloring**: Color by alignment blocks using `colorByBlocks` checkbox
- **Palette Selection**: Multiple color palette options (Spectral, Set1, Set2, Pastel)
- **Phylogenetic Integration**: Tree visualization through Archaeopteryx

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/MultipleAlignmentJmol.java:191-199](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/MultipleAlignmentJmol.java:294-306]()

### JmolPanel Core Integration

`JmolPanel` wraps the Jmol viewer and provides BioJava-specific functionality including structure loading, style management, and domain coloring capabilities.

| Style Option | Jmol Command Generated |
|--------------|------------------------|
| Cartoon | `cartoon on; ligand wireframe/spacefill` |
| Backbone | `backbone 0.4; cartoon off` |
| CPK | `cpk on; cartoon off` |
| Ball and Stick | `wireframe 0.2; spacefill 25%` |
| By Chain | `color_by_chain()` custom function |

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/JmolPanel.java:232-294]()

## Interactive Alignment Panels

### 2D Alignment Display Integration

The alignment panel system provides 2D sequence representations that synchronize with the 3D Jmol display. Selection in the 2D panel automatically highlights corresponding atoms in the 3D structure.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant AligPanel
    participant MouseListener
    participant JmolPanel
    participant JmolViewer
    
    User->>AligPanel: Mouse hover over position
    AligPanel->>MouseListener: mouseMoved()
    MouseListener->>AligPanel: getCurrentAlignedPosition()
    AligPanel->>AligPanel: updateJmolDisplay()
    AligPanel->>JmolPanel: evalString("select atoms...")
    JmolPanel->>JmolViewer: Execute selection command
    JmolViewer-->>User: Highlight atoms in 3D
```

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/aligpanel/AligPanel.java:426-479](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/aligpanel/MultipleAligPanel.java:350-373]()

### Mouse Interaction and Selection Management

Both `AligPanel` and `MultipleAligPanel` implement sophisticated mouse interaction through dedicated mouse listeners that support:

- **Hover Selection**: Real-time highlighting of alignment positions
- **Range Selection**: Click-and-drag to select alignment regions  
- **Toggle Selection**: Ctrl/Shift-click to modify selections
- **Selection Locking**: Persistent selections across multiple operations

The selection state is managed using `BitSet` objects that track selected alignment positions, with automatic translation to Jmol selection commands.

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/aligpanel/AligPanelMouseMotionListener.java:59-107](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/aligpanel/AligPanel.java:72-88]()

## Menu System and User Controls

### MenuCreator Functionality

The `MenuCreator` class provides standardized menu systems across all Jmol visualization windows, supporting common operations like file I/O, display options, and format exports.

Key menu categories:
- **File Menu**: Load, save, export PDB, print functionality
- **Align Menu**: New pairwise/multiple alignment launches
- **View Menu**: Text formats, alignment panels, distance matrices, dot plots
- **Help Menu**: Documentation and system information

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/MenuCreator.java:86-202]()

### Display Format Options

The visualization system supports multiple output formats through menu-driven actions:

| Format | Implementation | Purpose |
|--------|----------------|---------|
| Text Only | `AfpChainWriter.toWebSiteDisplay()` | Human-readable alignment |
| Aligned Pairs | `AfpChainWriter.toAlignedPairs()` | Residue-level correspondences |
| FatCat Format | `AFPChain.toFatcat()` | Algorithm-specific output |
| Distance Matrices | `getDistanceMatrices()` | Structural distance analysis |
| Phylogenetic Tree | `MultipleAlignmentTools.getKimuraTree()` | Evolutionary relationships |

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/StructureAlignmentJmol.java:373-414](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/MultipleAlignmentJmol.java:378-409]()

## Configuration and Customization

### Color Palette Management

The system uses `ColorBrewer` palettes for consistent coloring across multiple structures. Users can select from predefined palettes (Spectral, Set1, Set2, Pastel) that automatically scale to the number of structures being displayed.

### Jmol Script Generation

Alignment-specific Jmol scripts are generated dynamically based on alignment data and user preferences. The scripts handle:
- Residue selection based on alignment positions
- Color assignment using palette schemes  
- Ligand and metal ion highlighting
- Model-specific commands for multi-structure displays

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/MultipleAlignmentJmol.java:419-465](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/StructureAlignmentJmol.java:542-600]()

### Resource Management and Cleanup

All visualization components implement proper resource cleanup through `destroy()` methods that handle:
- Jmol viewer disposal
- Mouse listener removal  
- Structure object nullification
- Window listener cleanup

This ensures memory-efficient operation when working with multiple large structure alignments.

Sources: [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/AbstractAlignmentJmol.java:87-92](), [biojava-structure-gui/src/main/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/align/gui/jmol/JmolPanel.java:400-407]()

# Page: Protein Comparison Tool

# Protein Comparison Tool

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [biojava-protein-comparison-tool/pom.xml](biojava-protein-comparison-tool/pom.xml)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The Protein Comparison Tool is a standalone GUI application built on top of BioJava's structure analysis capabilities. It provides an interactive interface for comparing and aligning protein structures using BioJava's alignment algorithms. This tool is packaged as a self-contained JAR file that can be executed independently of other BioJava modules.

For information about the underlying Jmol integration and visualization components, see [Jmol Integration and Structure Visualization](#5.1). For details about the structural analysis algorithms used by this tool, see [Structural Analysis Tools](#3).

## Application Overview

The Protein Comparison Tool is implemented as a Maven module that creates a complete standalone application. The main entry point is the `AlignmentGui` class, which provides a graphical user interface for protein structure alignment and comparison tasks.

### Module Dependencies

The tool integrates multiple BioJava modules to provide comprehensive functionality:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Protein Comparison Tool"
        AlignmentGui["AlignmentGui<br/>(Main Class)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Dependencies"
        BioJavaCore["biojava-core<br/>(Base functionality)"]
        BioJavaStructure["biojava-structure<br/>(Structure processing)"]
        BioJavaAlignment["biojava-alignment<br/>(Alignment algorithms)"]
        BioJavaStructureGUI["biojava-structure-gui<br/>(GUI components)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Dependencies"
        Jmol["Jmol 13.0.14<br/>(3D visualization)"]
        Log4j["Log4J2<br/>(Logging framework)"]
        SLF4J["SLF4J<br/>(Logging API)"]
    end
    
    AlignmentGui --> BioJavaCore
    AlignmentGui --> BioJavaStructure
    AlignmentGui --> BioJavaAlignment
    AlignmentGui --> BioJavaStructureGUI
    AlignmentGui --> Jmol
    AlignmentGui --> Log4j
    AlignmentGui --> SLF4J
```

**Sources:** [biojava-protein-comparison-tool/pom.xml:28-80]()

The tool follows a layered architecture where the GUI layer leverages the underlying BioJava structure processing and alignment capabilities:

### Build Configuration Details

The build process includes several important configurations:

| Configuration | Purpose | Details |
|---------------|---------|---------|
| JAR Minimization | Disabled | Prevents removal of Jmol and Log4J dependencies |
| Vecmath Exclusion | Dependency conflict resolution | Excludes `javax/vecmath/**` from Jmol JAR |
| Demo Exclusion | Size optimization | Excludes demo classes from biojava-structure |
| Signature Exclusion | JAR validity | Removes META-INF signature files |
| Services Merging | Dependency integration | Merges META-INF/services files |

**Sources:** [biojava-protein-comparison-tool/pom.xml:94-141]()
