This document provides comprehensive information for developers working with BioJava, covering the build system architecture, testing infrastructure, continuous integration, and release management processes. It serves as a technical guide for contributors, maintainers, and developers who need to understand BioJava's development lifecycle and deployment procedures.

For information about BioJava's modular architecture and individual components, see [Build System and Module Structure](#6.1). For details about testing infrastructure and release processes, see [Testing, CI/CD, and Release Process](#6.2).

## Build System Architecture

BioJava uses a Maven-based multi-module build system orchestrated by a parent POM that manages dependencies, plugin versions, and build configurations across all modules. The build system supports Java 11+ compatibility and provides comprehensive tooling for development, testing, and deployment.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Maven Parent POM"
        ParentPOM["pom.xml<br/>GroupId: org.biojava<br/>ArtifactId: biojava"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Modules"
        Core["biojava-core<br/>Foundation classes"]
        Alignment["biojava-alignment<br/>Sequence alignment"]
        Structure["biojava-structure<br/>3D structure processing"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Specialized Modules"
        StructureGUI["biojava-structure-gui<br/>Jmol integration"]
        Genome["biojava-genome<br/>Genomics tools"]
        ProteinTool["biojava-protein-comparison-tool<br/>GUI application"]
        ModFinder["biojava-modfinder<br/>Modifications"]
        AAProps["biojava-aa-prop<br/>Amino acid properties"]
        Disorder["biojava-protein-disorder<br/>Disorder prediction"]
        Survival["biojava-survival<br/>Statistical analysis"]
        Ontology["biojava-ontology<br/>Ontology support"]
        WS["biojava-ws<br/>Web services"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Testing Module"
        IntegrationTest["biojava-integrationtest<br/>Integration tests"]
    end
    
    ParentPOM --> Core
    ParentPOM --> Alignment
    ParentPOM --> Structure
    ParentPOM --> StructureGUI
    ParentPOM --> Genome
    ParentPOM --> ProteinTool
    ParentPOM --> ModFinder
    ParentPOM --> AAProps
    ParentPOM --> Disorder
    ParentPOM --> Survival
    ParentPOM --> Ontology
    ParentPOM --> WS
    ParentPOM --> IntegrationTest
    
    Core --> Structure
    Core --> Alignment
    Structure --> StructureGUI
    Structure --> ProteinTool
    Structure --> ModFinder
    Structure --> AAProps
    Core --> Genome
    Core --> WS
```

The parent POM defines critical build properties including Java version compatibility, dependency versions, and plugin configurations. Key build properties include `jdk.version` set to 11, UTF-8 encoding for all sources, and standardized logging frameworks.

**Sources:** [pom.xml:34-48](), [pom.xml:721-737]()

## Maven Plugin Management

The build system employs extensive plugin management to ensure consistent builds across all modules. Essential plugins include the Maven Compiler Plugin for Java 11 compilation, Surefire Plugin for unit testing, and Failsafe Plugin for integration testing.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Build Plugins"
        Compiler["maven-compiler-plugin<br/>v3.13.0<br/>Java 11 target"]
        Jar["maven-jar-plugin<br/>v3.4.2<br/>Manifest generation"]
        Source["maven-source-plugin<br/>v3.3.1<br/>Source JARs"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Testing Plugins"
        Surefire["maven-surefire-plugin<br/>v3.5.2<br/>Unit tests"]
        Failsafe["maven-failsafe-plugin<br/>v3.0.0-M5<br/>Integration tests"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Quality Plugins"
        Checkstyle["maven-checkstyle-plugin<br/>v3.1.1<br/>Code style"]
        Javadoc["maven-javadoc-plugin<br/>v3.11.2<br/>Documentation"]
        Enforcer["maven-enforcer-plugin<br/>v3.5.0<br/>Build rules"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Release Plugins"
        Release["maven-release-plugin<br/>v3.1.1<br/>Version management"]
        GPG["maven-gpg-plugin<br/>v1.6<br/>Code signing"]
        Nexus["nexus-staging-maven-plugin<br/>v1.6.13<br/>Maven Central"]
    end
```

The Surefire plugin is configured with increased memory allocation (`-Xmx1500M`) and fork settings to handle BioJava's memory-intensive tests. The Jar plugin includes manifest entries for trusted library status and permissions required for some BioJava applications.

**Sources:** [pom.xml:169-347](), [pom.xml:350-403]()

## Dependency Management Strategy

BioJava implements centralized dependency management through the parent POM's `dependencyManagement` section, ensuring version consistency across all modules. Critical dependencies include JUnit 5 for testing, SLF4J 2.0 for logging, and specialized libraries like MMTF for molecular structure formats.

| Dependency Category | Key Libraries | Versions |
|-------------------|---------------|----------|
| Testing Framework | JUnit Jupiter, JUnit Vintage | 5.10.1 |
| Logging | SLF4J API, Log4j Core | 2.0.12, 2.23.1 |
| Structure Formats | MMTF API, CIFTools Java | 1.0.11, 7.0.1 |
| XML Processing | Jakarta XML Bind, JAXB Runtime | 4.0.0, 4.0.3 |
| Utilities | Google Guava | 33.4.0-jre |

Logging is standardized on SLF4J 2.0 with Log4j 2 as the implementation, providing consistent logging across all modules while allowing flexibility in logging configuration.

**Sources:** [pom.xml:415-492](), [pom.xml:42-47]()

## Continuous Integration Pipeline

BioJava uses GitHub Actions for continuous integration with separate workflows for pull requests and master branch builds. The CI system tests compatibility across multiple JDK versions and operating systems.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Pull Request Workflow"
        PRTrigger["PR or Push to Feature Branch"]
        PRMatrix["Test Matrix<br/>JDK: 17, 21<br/>OS: Ubuntu, Windows"]
        PRBuild["mvn verify --no-transfer-progress"]
        PRJava11["Special JDK 11 Test<br/>Zulu Distribution"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Master Branch Workflow"
        MasterTrigger["Push to Master"]
        MasterTest["JDK 21 Ubuntu Test"]
        MasterBuild["mvn verify -pl '!biojava-integrationtest'"]
        SonarQube["SonarCloud Analysis<br/>Code Quality Metrics"]
    end
    
    PRTrigger --> PRMatrix
    PRMatrix --> PRBuild
    PRTrigger --> PRJava11
    
    MasterTrigger --> MasterTest
    MasterTest --> MasterBuild
    MasterBuild --> SonarQube
```

The pull request workflow tests on JDK 17 and 21 with both Ubuntu and Windows, ensuring cross-platform compatibility. A separate job tests JDK 11 using the Zulu distribution since OpenJDK 11 is not available in GitHub Actions.

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/pull_request.yml:14-35](), [.github/workflows/master.yml:12-37]()

## Testing Infrastructure

BioJava implements a comprehensive testing strategy with both unit tests and integration tests. Unit tests run with every build, while integration tests are executed separately due to their longer execution time and external dependencies.

The integration test module (`biojava-integrationtest`) is configured to skip JAR creation since it only contains test code. Integration tests can include network operations, such as testing URL-based file parsing for remote structure files.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Unit Testing"
        JUnit4["JUnit 4<br/>Legacy tests"]
        JUnit5["JUnit 5<br/>New tests"]
        Vintage["JUnit Vintage Engine<br/>Backward compatibility"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integration Testing"
        IntegrationModule["biojava-integrationtest<br/>Separate module"]
        NetworkTests["URL-based parsing<br/>External dependencies"]
        SlowTests["Long-running tests<br/>Performance validation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Test Configuration"
        SurefireConfig["Surefire Plugin<br/>-Xmx1500M<br/>reuseForks: false"]
        FailsafeConfig["Failsafe Plugin<br/>mvn verify target"]
    end
    
    JUnit4 --> Vintage
    JUnit5 --> Vintage
    Vintage --> SurefireConfig
    IntegrationModule --> FailsafeConfig
    NetworkTests --> IntegrationModule
    SlowTests --> IntegrationModule
```

The test configuration allocates 1.5GB of memory for unit tests and disables fork reuse to prevent memory issues during testing. Integration tests are executed only during the Maven `verify` phase.

**Sources:** [pom.xml:353-361](), [biojava-integrationtest/pom.xml:70-83](), [biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/io/TestURLBasedFileParsing.java:37-44]()

## Release Management Process

BioJava follows a formal release process using Maven Release Plugin with deployment to Maven Central via OSS Sonatype. The release process includes automated version management, code signing, and artifact deployment.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Release Preparation"
        PrepareCmd["mvn -Prelease release:prepare"]
        VersionBump["Automatic version increment"]
        GitTag["Git tag creation"]
        PomUpdate["POM version updates"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Release Execution"
        PerformCmd["mvn -Prelease release:perform"]
        Build["Clean build with release profile"]
        Sign["GPG artifact signing"]
        Deploy["Deploy to OSS Sonatype"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Artifact Generation"
        MainJar["Main JAR files"]
        SourceJar["Source JARs<br/>maven-source-plugin"]
        JavadocJar["Javadoc JARs<br/>maven-javadoc-plugin"]
        Signatures["GPG signatures<br/>maven-gpg-plugin"]
    end
    
    PrepareCmd --> VersionBump
    VersionBump --> GitTag
    GitTag --> PomUpdate
    PomUpdate --> PerformCmd
    PerformCmd --> Build
    Build --> Sign
    Sign --> Deploy
    Build --> MainJar
    Build --> SourceJar
    Build --> JavadocJar
    Sign --> Signatures
```

The release profile activates additional plugins including GPG signing, source JAR creation, and Javadoc generation. The Nexus Staging Plugin handles the deployment to Maven Central with automatic release after staging validation.

**Sources:** [pom.xml:574-668](), [README.md:40-46]()

## Development Profile Configuration

BioJava provides multiple build profiles to support different development scenarios. The main profiles include the default profile for development builds, a release profile for Maven Central deployment, and a codesigning profile for signed JARs.

| Profile Name | Purpose | Key Features |
|-------------|---------|--------------|
| Default | Development builds | Standard compilation, testing |
| Release | Maven Central deployment | GPG signing, source JARs, Javadoc |
| Codesigning | Signed JAR generation | Timestamp signing, keystore configuration |

The release profile includes comprehensive artifact generation with source attachments, Javadoc generation, and GPG signing for security. The codesigning profile supports timestamp signing with external timestamp authorities for long-term signature validity.

**Sources:** [pom.xml:575-719](), [pom.xml:674-718]()

## Documentation Generation

BioJava generates comprehensive documentation using Maven Site Plugin with aggregate Javadoc generation across all modules. The documentation build creates unified API documentation and project reports.

The Javadoc configuration includes custom footer with Google Analytics tracking and allows script content in comments. The aggregate reporting generates a single documentation site containing all module documentation.

**Sources:** [pom.xml:494-550](), [pom.xml:231-245]()

This document provides a comprehensive guide to BioJava's Maven-based build system, including its multi-module architecture, dependency management, and build configurations. It covers the project structure, module dependencies, build profiles, and release processes for developers working with or contributing to the BioJava codebase.

For information about testing infrastructure and CI/CD processes, see [Testing, CI/CD, and Release Process](#6.2).

## Maven Multi-Module Architecture

BioJava uses Apache Maven as its primary build tool with a multi-module project structure. The parent POM coordinates all modules and provides shared configuration, dependency management, and build profiles.

### Module Dependency Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    Parent["biojava (Parent POM)"] --> Core["biojava-core"]
    Parent --> Alignment["biojava-alignment"]
    Parent --> Structure["biojava-structure"]
    Parent --> StructureGUI["biojava-structure-gui"]
    Parent --> Genome["biojava-genome"]
    Parent --> ModFinder["biojava-modfinder"]
    Parent --> WS["biojava-ws"]
    Parent --> ProteinDisorder["biojava-protein-disorder"]
    Parent --> AAProp["biojava-aa-prop"]
    Parent --> Survival["biojava-survival"]
    Parent --> Ontology["biojava-ontology"]
    Parent --> ProteinTool["biojava-protein-comparison-tool"]
    Parent --> IntegrationTest["biojava-integrationtest"]
    
    Core --> Alignment
    Core --> Structure
    Core --> Genome
    Core --> WS
    Core --> ProteinDisorder
    Alignment --> Structure
    Alignment --> Genome
    Structure --> StructureGUI
    Structure --> ModFinder
    Structure --> AAProp
    Structure --> IntegrationTest
```

**Module Dependency Relationships**
The dependency hierarchy shows `biojava-core` as the foundation module, with specialized modules building upon it and each other.

Sources: [pom.xml:721-737](), [biojava-structure/pom.xml:52-62](), [biojava-genome/pom.xml:71-81]()

## Project Configuration

The parent POM defines critical build properties and dependency versions used across all modules:

| Property | Value | Purpose |
|----------|-------|---------|

| `project.build.sourceEncoding` | UTF-8 | Source file encoding |
| `mmtf.version` | 1.0.11 | MMTF library version |
| `slf4j.version` | 2.0.12 | Logging framework version |
| `ciftools.version` | 7.0.1 | CIF parsing library version |

```mermaid
    Plugins --> Surefire["Surefire 3.5.2"]
    Plugins --> Javadoc["Javadoc 3.11.2"]
```

**Global Configuration Management**
Maven properties provide centralized version management across all modules.

Sources: [pom.xml:34-48](), [pom.xml:170-346]()

## Dependency Management

### Centralized Dependency Management

The parent POM uses `dependencyManagement` to control versions across all modules:

```mermaid
graph TD
    ParentPOM["Parent POM"] --> DepMgmt["dependencyManagement"]
    DepMgmt --> JUnit["JUnit 4.13.2 & JUnit 5.10.1"]
    DepMgmt --> Logging["SLF4J 2.0.12 + Log4J 2.23.1"]
    DepMgmt --> XML["Jakarta XML Bind 4.0.0"]
    DepMgmt --> Guava["Google Guava 33.4.0"]
    DepMgmt --> Forester["BioJava Forester 1.039"]
    
    JUnit --> Modules["Child Modules"]
    Logging --> Modules
    XML --> Modules
    Guava --> Modules
    Forester --> Modules
```

**Dependency Version Control**
The parent POM ensures consistent dependency versions across all modules without requiring version specification in child POMs.

Sources: [pom.xml:415-492]()

### Logging Configuration

All modules use SLF4J with Log4J2 binding:

- **API**: `slf4j-api` (version managed in parent)
- **Implementation**: `log4j-slf4j2-impl` + `log4j-core` + `log4j-api`
- **Scope**: Runtime for implementation dependencies

Sources: [pom.xml:443-469](), [biojava-core/pom.xml:58-75]()

## Module-Specific Configurations

### Core Module Dependencies

Each module has specific dependency requirements:

| Module | Key Dependencies |
|--------|------------------|
| `biojava-structure` | MMTF, CifTools, JGraphT, Jackson, Vecmath |
| `biojava-structure-gui` | Jmol 14.31.10, JColorBrewer |
| `biojava-genome` | Google Guava |
| `biojava-ws` | JSON-lib |

### JAR Packaging Configuration

All modules exclude demo packages from final JARs to avoid namespace conflicts:

```xml
<excludes>
    <exclude>demo/**</exclude>
</excludes>
```

# Page: Testing, CI/CD, and Release Process

# Testing, CI/CD, and Release Process

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/workflows/master.yml](.github/workflows/master.yml)
- [.github/workflows/pull_request.yml](.github/workflows/pull_request.yml)
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)
- [README.md](README.md)
- [biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/io/TestURLBasedFileParsing.java](biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/io/TestURLBasedFileParsing.java)

</details>



This document covers BioJava's testing infrastructure, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, and release management processes. It details the automated workflows that ensure code quality, the testing strategies across multiple Java versions and platforms, and the procedures for publishing new versions to Maven Central.

For information about the build system and module structure, see [Module Structure](#6.1).

## Testing Infrastructure

BioJava employs a comprehensive testing strategy using JUnit 4 for unit testing and Maven for test execution. The testing framework supports both unit tests and integration tests, with the ability to exclude integration tests for faster CI builds.

### Test Structure and Organization

The project uses standard JUnit 4 annotations and follows Maven's conventional directory structure for tests. Test classes are located in `src/test/java` directories within each module and follow naming conventions that mirror the main source structure.

**Example Test Structure:**
```
biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/io/TestURLBasedFileParsing.java
```

Tests utilize standard JUnit patterns with `@Test` annotations and assertion methods like `assertNotNull()` for validation [biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/io/TestURLBasedFileParsing.java:29-43]().

### Test Execution Strategy

The Maven build system supports different test execution modes:
- **Full verification**: `mvn verify` runs all tests including integration tests
- **Excluding integration tests**: `mvn verify -pl '!biojava-integrationtest'` for faster CI builds
- **No transfer progress**: `--no-transfer-progress` flag reduces log verbosity in CI environments

Sources: [.github/workflows/pull_request.yml](), [.github/workflows/master.yml](), [biojava-structure/src/test/java/org/biojava/nbio/structure/io/TestURLBasedFileParsing.java]()

## Continuous Integration Pipeline

BioJava uses GitHub Actions for continuous integration with separate workflows for pull requests and master branch commits. The CI system tests multiple Java versions and operating systems to ensure compatibility across different environments.

### CI Workflow Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph PR["Pull Request Workflow"]
        PROrig["Push to non-master branch"] --> PRBuild["pull_request.yml"]
        PRtoMaster["PR to master"] --> PRBuild
        PRBuild --> PRMatrix["Test Matrix"]
        
        subgraph PRMatrix["PR Test Matrix"]
            PRJava11["Java 11 (Zulu)"]
            PRJava17["Java 17 (Oracle)"] 
            PRJava21["Java 21 (Oracle)"]
            PRUbuntu["Ubuntu Latest"]
            PRWindows["Windows Latest"]
        end
        
        PRMatrix --> PRVerify["mvn verify --no-transfer-progress"]
    end
    
    subgraph Master["Master Branch Workflow"]
        MasterPush["Push to master"] --> MasterBuild["master.yml"]
        MasterBuild --> MasterTest["Java 21 Ubuntu"]
        MasterTest --> MasterVerifyAnalyze["mvn verify + SonarQube"]
        MasterVerifyAnalyze --> SonarCloud["SonarCloud Analysis"]
    end
    
    subgraph TestExecution["Test Execution"]
        PRVerify --> UnitTests["Unit Tests"]
        PRVerify --> IntegrationTests["Integration Tests"]
        MasterVerifyAnalyze --> UnitTestsOnly["Unit Tests Only"]
        MasterVerifyAnalyze --> CodeCoverage["Code Coverage"]
    end
```

### Multi-Platform Testing Strategy

The pull request workflow tests across multiple configurations:

| Java Version | Distribution | Operating Systems |
|--------------|-------------|-------------------|
| 11 | Zulu | Ubuntu Latest |
| 17 | Oracle | Ubuntu Latest, Windows Latest |
| 21 | Oracle | Ubuntu Latest, Windows Latest |

The master branch workflow focuses on a single configuration (Java 21 on Ubuntu) but includes additional code quality analysis.

### SonarQube Integration

The master branch workflow integrates with SonarQube for code quality analysis [.github/workflows/master.yml:34-37](). The analysis uses:
- `SONAR_TOKEN` and `SONAR_HOST_URL` secrets for authentication
- `sonar.projectKey=biojava_biojava` for project identification
- `sonar.organization=biojava` for organization grouping

Sources: [.github/workflows/pull_request.yml](), [.github/workflows/master.yml]()

## Release Process

BioJava follows a structured release process using Maven's release plugin and semantic versioning. The process includes preparation, publishing to Maven Central, and documentation updates.

### Release Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Preparation["Release Preparation"]
        ReleasePrepare["mvn -Prelease release:prepare"]
        ReleasePrepare --> VersionBump["Version Bump"]
        ReleasePrepare --> TagCreation["Git Tag Creation"]
        ReleasePrepare --> POMUpdate["POM Updates"]
    end
    
    subgraph Publishing["Publication"]
        ReleasePerform["mvn -Prelease release:perform"]
        ReleasePerform --> MavenCentral["Deploy to Maven Central"]
        MavenCentral --> Validation["Artifact Validation"]
    end
    
    subgraph Documentation["Documentation Update"]
        SiteGeneration["mvn -Prelease site"]
        SiteGeneration --> JavadocBuild["target/site/apidocs"]
        JavadocBuild --> GitHubPages["biojava.github.io repo"]
        GitHubPages --> APILinking["Link docs/api to docs/apiM.m.p"]
    end
    
    subgraph ChangelogUpdate["Changelog Management"]
        ReleaseNotes["Update CHANGELOG.md"]
        ReleaseNotes --> VersionSection["Add version section"]
        VersionSection --> ChangeCategories["Fixed/Added/Breaking/Removed"]
    end
    
    Preparation --> Publishing
    Publishing --> Documentation
    Documentation --> ChangelogUpdate
```

### Maven Release Commands

The release process uses Maven profiles and plugins:

1. **Preparation Phase**: `mvn -Prelease release:prepare`
   - Updates version numbers in POMs
   - Creates Git tags
   - Commits changes

2. **Performance Phase**: `mvn -Prelease release:perform`
   - Builds artifacts
   - Deploys to Maven Central
   - Validates deployment

3. **Documentation Phase**: `mvn -Prelease site`
   - Generates Javadocs in `target/site`
   - Requires manual deployment to GitHub Pages

### Javadoc Publishing Process

Documentation publishing involves multiple steps:
1. Generate site with `mvn -Prelease site`
2. Extract contents from `target/site/apidocs`
3. Push to `biojava.github.io` repository under `docs/apiM.m.p` directory structure
4. Update symbolic link from `docs/api` to current version directory

Sources: [README.md:40-46]()

## Version Management and Release History

BioJava follows semantic versioning with a comprehensive changelog documenting all changes. The versioning strategy has evolved to support major compatibility requirements.

### Version Evolution Timeline

```mermaid
timeline
    title "BioJava Version Evolution"
    
    section Java 6/7 Era
        BioJava 3.0.7 : GenBank parser
                      : Basic features
        BioJava 3.0.8 : ASA calculation
                      : SCOP improvements
        BioJava 3.1.0 : CE-CP algorithm
                      : FASTQ improvements
    
    section Java 8 Transition
        BioJava 4.0.0 : Major API changes
                      : SLF4J logging
                      : Maven Central
        BioJava 4.2.0 : Secondary structure
                      : Multiple alignments
                      : CE-Symm algorithm
    
    section Modern Era
        BioJava 5.0.0 : mmCIF data model
                      : MMTF support
                      : Java 8 required
        BioJava 6.0.0 : API cleanup
                      : CIF improvements
                      : Binary CIF support
    
    section Current
        BioJava 7.0.0 : Java 11 required
                      : Security fixes
        BioJava 7.2.2 : Performance improvements
                      : mmCIF enhancements
```

### Changelog Structure

The changelog follows a consistent format with categorized changes:

- **Fixed**: Bug fixes and corrections
- **Added**: New features and capabilities  
- **Breaking**: API changes requiring code updates
- **Removed**: Deprecated functionality removal

### Java Compatibility Timeline

| Version Range | Java Requirement | Key Changes |
|---------------|------------------|-------------|
| 3.x | Java 6, 7 | Legacy compatibility |
| 4.x | Java 6, 7, 8 | Transition period |
| 5.x | Java 8+ | Modern features |
| 6.x | Java 8+ | API stabilization |
| 7.x | Java 11+ | Current LTS requirement |

### Recent Release Pattern

Recent releases show focus on:
- mmCIF parsing performance improvements [CHANGELOG.md:7-8]()
- Dependency upgrades for security [CHANGELOG.md:128,136,141]()
- Edge case handling in file parsing [CHANGELOG.md:18-19,27-28]()
- Code quality improvements via SonarQube integration

Sources: [CHANGELOG.md]()
